'''Estelle Lucille Basor''' (born 1947){{r|born}} is an American mathematician interested in [[operator theory]] and the theory of [[random matrix|random matrices]]. She is professor emeritus of mathematics at the [[California Polytechnic State University]] (Cal Poly),{{r|calpoly}} and deputy director of the [[American Institute of Mathematics]].{{r|cv}}

==Education and career==
Basor earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics from the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]] in 1969, and completed a Ph.D. there in 1975.{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, supervised by [[Harold Widom]], was ''Asymptotic Formulas for Toeplitz Determinants''.{{r|mgp}}

She joined the Cal Poly faculty in 1976, and taught there until retiring in 2008.{{r|cv|calpoly}}

She served as an [[American Mathematical Society]] Council member at large from 2011 to 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS Committees |url=http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/mal-past.html |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref>

==Recognition==
At Cal Poly, she was the 2005 winner of the Distinguished Research, Creative Activity and Professional Development Award, and a colloquium in her and professor Rami Shani’s honor was held in 2006.{{r|colloq}} She was elected to the 2018 class of [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].{{r|fams}}

==Personal life==
Basor's husband,{{r|sentinel}} Kent E. Morrison, is also a mathematician who went to school with her at Santa Cruz, worked with her at Cal Poly, and is now associated with the American Institute of Mathematics.{{r|morrison}}
